paper-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the paper role.

panel.purpose: Toolbars, sticky heads, banners, empty states, and the "you" row in the season table.

panel-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the panel grey role.

sunken.purpose: Wells, bar tracks, disabled fills, hover grounds.

sunken-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the sunken grey role.

ink.purpose: Primary text, and the selected fill — the system's one high-contrast event.

ink-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the ink role.

ink-on.purpose: Text and marks sitting on an --ink fill. Inverts locally; never substitute a page-relative neutral here.

ink-on-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the ink on (reversed) role.

n-1.purpose: Supporting copy, inactive nav, team full names. 5.4:1 on paper, 7.0:1 on graphite.

n-1-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the secondary text role.

n-2.purpose: Metadata and de-emphasis. Only at 14px or bold.

n-2-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the tertiary text role.

n-3.purpose: Input borders, scrollbar thumb, the @ glyph, an em-dash for a missing pick.

n-3-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the strong rule role.

rule.purpose: The workhorse hairline separator — every list, table row, header and tile boundary.

rule-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the hairline role.

correct.purpose: A right pick, an active invite key, a success notice.

correct-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the correct green role.

correct-soft-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the correct wash role.

wrong.purpose: A wrong pick, a form error, the admin sync-error panel.

wrong-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the wrong red role.

wrong-soft-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the wrong wash role.

live.purpose: A game actually in progress — the pulsing dot, the in-progress score.

live-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the live amber role.

live-soft-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the live wash role.

focus.purpose: The focus ring and the caret. The one blue in the system, so a keyboard ring is never mistaken for content.

focus-dark.purpose: Dark-theme value for the focus blue role.

display.purpose: Declared as --fs-display (40px → 44px) and reserved for a single dominant number. Not currently used by any shipped screen.

headline.purpose: h1 — one per page, always inside a .rule-head.

subtitle.purpose: h3, the team abbreviation in a pick side, the header wordmark.

body.purpose: The UI default. Paragraphs cap at --measure (68ch).

meta.purpose: The density workhorse — timestamps, spreads, counts, consensus names, table cells.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked micro-label. Column heads, section meta, state chips. The system's one typographic mannerism.

numeric.purpose: JetBrains Mono with tabular figures, for any number that sits in a column with other numbers.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default for every hover, focus, selection and ground change. Applied per-property, never to `all`.

motion.name: state-slow
motion.purpose: Upper bound for a state transition. Nothing in this system animates longer than this except the two ambient loops below.

motion.name: live-pulse
motion.purpose: The dot beside a game actually in progress. Reports state; it is not decoration.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Skeleton for content that is arriving, used instead of a spinner.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Everything collapses under prefers-reduced-motion. No exceptions.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Consensus strip goes one column → two; stat tiles 2-up → 4-up.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Desktop top nav appears, fixed bottom tab bar disappears, shell padding 16px → 32px.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The whole type scale steps up one notch.

containers.name: picking-column
containers.purpose: The pick list is measured rather than full-bleed — a stretched row puts the team name a long way from its score.

containers.name: measure
containers.purpose: Paragraph cap, applied to every `p` in base.

narrative.overview:
This is a record book for one group's season, not a betting product. The week is a dense ruled ledger: games run down the page, members run across it, and the rules between them carry the structure that a card grid would otherwise fake. Nothing here is trying to sell a wager — it is trying to let ten friends see, quickly and exactly, who took which side and who was right.

The direction is Swiss utility, pinned by the owner from three previewed options against one binding constraint: it must not look vibecoded. In practice that means a near-monochrome ground, hairlines as the only separator, one sans on a fixed scale, tracked 11px uppercase labels, tabular numerals everywhere a number sits in a column, and square geometry. Team colour is the sole saturated element on the page, and it never appears as decoration.

The mode is Operate. The visitor is doing a task — getting through a week of games in a spare minute on a phone, or reading the group against itself at 02:15 on a Tuesday when a Monday-night game finally ends in Germany. Scanability and certainty outrank expression. The personality lives in precision: the way a spread is replaced in place by a score, the way a losing side recedes, the way the corner badge on your pick changes from "this is mine" to "this was right".
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome paper-and-ink ground in both themes; the dark theme is warm graphite, not black.
Hairline rules do the structural work that shadows do elsewhere. There is not one box-shadow in the codebase.
One type family (Inter), with JetBrains Mono reserved for digits that must line up.
Fixed type steps at roughly 1.2, never fluid, stepping up one notch above 1024px.
Team colour is encoded information only — consensus bars, grid abbreviations, pick strips.
Square by default; the only radius is 3px.
Authored 16-unit SVG icon set. No emoji, no icon font.

rules.name: The Team Colour Rule
rules.body: Team colour is the only saturated colour in the interface, and it appears only where it encodes something: the consensus bars on /standings and a profile, the team abbreviation in a grid cell, the abbreviation in a post-kickoff consensus strip. Never as a background, never as an accent, never to make a section look livelier.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Every team colour ships as a resolved pair. teamColors() takes whichever of the primary/alternate pair reads better and walks it toward white or black until it clears 3:1 against that specific ground. Both values travel inline as --tc-l / --tc-d; CSS picks one. A unit test asserts all 32 primaries clear the bar on both grounds. The ground constants in lib/nfl/colors.ts are hard-coded copies of --paper and its dark value; changing either token means changing LIGHT_GROUND / DARK_GROUND too.

rules.name: The Inverted Ground Rule
rules.body: A selected pick button is filled with --ink, which inverts locally — in dark mode that is a light button on a dark page. Anything inside it must use --ink-on and its alpha steps, never the page-relative neutrals, or it drops below contrast in exactly one of the two themes. Team logos take onInverted on <TeamLogo>, which flips which of ESPN's two renderings is displayed.

rules.name: The Warm Graphite Rule
rules.body: The dark ground is #1a1917 — lifted well off #000 so the page reads as a ground rather than a void, and warm so it stays the same paper-and-ink world as the light theme instead of becoming a separate cold one. Never darken it toward black.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Inter for everything. JetBrains Mono only where digits must line up: scores, records, percentages, invite keys, clock times, season numbers. If a number is prose rather than data, it stays in Inter.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number in this app sits in a column with other numbers. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is on every table, every .tnum, and every element marked data-numeric. Mark the element rather than eyeballing whether it will ever be compared.

rules.name: The Sixteen Pixel Rule
rules.body: Form inputs are 16px, never smaller. Anything under 16px makes iOS Safari zoom on focus, and this pool is used on a phone more than anywhere else.

rules.name: The One Mannerism Rule
rules.body: .label is the single typographic flourish the system allows. Do not invent a second one — no small caps, no letterspaced body, no italic meta.

rules.name: The Live Edge Rule
rules.body: Any horizontal scroller wears .edge-fade, which masks the last 28px so a cut-off column reads as "there is more" rather than as a broken layout. The mask is removed via data-at-end="true" once the scroller bottoms out.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Interactive targets are at least 44px. Below 768px primary navigation is a fixed bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding, clear of the iOS home indicator; body carries the same inset so content never hides beneath it.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never add a box-shadow, a drop-shadow, or a glow. If something needs to separate from its surroundings, give it a rule; if it needs to sit above, give it Panel.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: Paper → Panel → Sunken is the entire elevation vocabulary. There is no fourth surface. A design that seems to need one is usually a card grid in disguise.

rules.name: The Three Pixel Rule
rules.body: Radii are 3px or 0. Nothing in this app is rounded-lg, rounded-xl, or rounded-2xl. A pill radius is permitted only on something that is genuinely a dot or a track.

rules.name: The Authored Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons are hand-drawn SVG on the 16-unit grid in components/icons.tsx. No emoji, no unicode glyphs as iconography, no icon font, no icons. Icons are aria-hidden by default and become labelled graphics only when passed a title.

dos: Do separate with a 1px --rule hairline first. Reach for Panel only when a surface genuinely needs to sit above the page.
Do put every number that could ever appear beside another number in JetBrains Mono with data-numeric.
Do use --ink fill to mean selected, in every context — pick side, week cell, sort chip. It is the system's one high-contrast event and it must mean one thing.
Do supply both --tc-l and --tc-d via teamColorVars() whenever team colour is used, and let .team-fill / .team-text choose. Never write a team hex directly into markup.
Do switch to --ink-on and its alpha steps inside anything filled with --ink, and pass onInverted to <TeamLogo> there.

Do keep base element styles in @layer base and shared classes in @layer components. Cascade layers are load-bearing here: unlayered CSS outranks everything Tailwind emits regardless of specificity, and an unlayered button { color: inherit } silently beat every text-* utility until this was fixed.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces — selection, caret, accent, scrollbar, focus ring, underline offset. The parts we did not draw still belong to the system.
Do give any horizontal scroller .edge-fade and any tall table a sticky left-0 first column on a bg-paper fill.

Do keep motion at 150–250ms and confine it to state transitions. The only two authored moments are .live-dot and .skeleton — both report state rather than decorate. Everything collapses under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't add a shadow, glow, or gradient header. There are none in the codebase and there is no case that needs the first one.
Don't use glassmorphism. The 2px backdrop blur on the two fixed bars is the ceiling.
Don't build page structure out of same-size feature cards. Cards are for objects that are genuinely cards.
Don't use emoji or unicode glyphs as iconography. Add to components/icons.tsx on the 16-unit grid instead.
Don't exceed a 3px radius. Nothing is rounded-2xl.
Don't use team colour as decoration, as a section background, or as an accent. Only where it encodes which team.
Don't put a page-relative neutral (--n-1, --n-2, --n-3) inside an --ink fill. It will fail contrast in exactly one theme, and it will be the theme you did not test.
Don't make type fluid or introduce a second font family. The scale is fixed; the step-up at 1024px is the entire responsive type story.
Don't set a form input below 16px.
Don't change --paper or the dark ground without updating LIGHT_GROUND / DARK_GROUND in lib/nfl/colors.ts and the themeColor viewport entries in app/layout.tsx. Three places, one value.
